newsitem.title: UK: Horlick hoping for settlement with MGAM.
newsitem.headline: Horlick hoping for settlement with MGAM.

text.p: Nicola Horlick remains hopeful of an amicable resolution of her dispute with former employer Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) but is still considering legal action if none can be reached, her lawyer said on Monday.

"She is still hopeful that there might be an amicable resolution. If she is not able to get a quick and amicable resolution then she is still looking at legal action on the grounds that she was constructively dismissed," John Farr, a partner at law firm Herbert Smith, said.

Farr told reporters at the firm's London offices that Horlick, who resigned from her post as head of British pension fund business following her suspension by MGAM last Tuesday for an alleged breach of contract, said his client's first priority was to get her job back.

Horlick had been promised by MGAM's German parent Deutsche Bank "that the matter would be looked into", Farr said. The 35-year-old fund manager made a whirlwind visit to Deutsche's Frankfurt headquarters last Friday after she failed to meet her MGAM bosses in London.

Farr said that if Horlick did not get her job back then she wanted compensation. He said Horlick wanted the matter resolved as quickly as possible, adding he hoped this could be "within the week or the next few days".

The lawyer said newspaper reports that Horlick, who has been accused by MGAM of trying to lure colleagues to leave with her for a rival firm, was talking to MGAM clients about a move were "totally untrue".
